title: MetaLLM: A High-performant and Cost-efficient Dynamic Framework for Wrapping LLMs
summary: MetaLLM wraps a pool of LLMs and learns, per query, which model to call by treating selection as a multi-armed bandit whose reward trades accuracy against price. Experiments on classification and multiple-choice QA use commercial APIs (OpenAI, Together AI) and open models.
key_idea: Bandit-based per-query LLM selection trading off accuracy and API cost.
relevance_rationale: Seed paper for online, bandit-feedback query routing with explicit cost term.

title: Adaptive LLM Routing under Budget Constraints
summary: PILOT casts LLM routing as a contextual bandit: a shared query/LLM embedding space is pretrained from offline human preference data and then refined online with LinUCB-style updates from partial feedback. An online cost policy framed as a multi-choice knapsack enforces per-user budgets.
key_idea: Preference-prior-informed LinUCB plus knapsack cost policy for budgeted online routing.
relevance_rationale: Core C5 seed: combines offline preference data with online bandit feedback under budgets.
found_via: ti:"Adaptive LLM Routing under Budget Constraints"

title: LLM Bandit: Cost-Efficient LLM Generation via Preference-Conditioned Dynamic Routing
summary: Formulates LLM selection as a multi-armed bandit whose policy is conditioned on a user-supplied performance/cost preference at inference time, and is designed to generalize to LLMs not seen in training. Reports accuracy and cost gains across several LLM platforms.
key_idea: Preference-conditioned bandit routing that lets operators dial cost vs quality at inference.
relevance_rationale: Seed paper; online routing with tunable cost trade-off and new-model generalization.

title: Online Cascade Learning for Efficient Inference over Streams
cost_reduction_reported: LLM-level accuracy while cutting inference cost by as much as 90% (four stream benchmarks)
summary: Learns a cascade online over a data stream: cheap models (e.g. logistic regression) are updated by imitating LLM outputs collected on deferred items, and a deferral policy decides which model answers. Posed as imitation learning with a no-regret guarantee; robust to input distribution shift.
key_idea: Online imitation-learned cascade where cheap models learn from LLM answers on the fly.
relevance_rationale: Seed; online learning of a cost-saving cascade from live traffic with drift robustness.

title: Cost-Effective Online Multi-LLM Selection with Versatile Reward Models
benchmarks: three application scenarios with nine LLMs
summary: C2MAB-V is a cost-aware combinatorial bandit that picks a set of LLMs per task under versatile reward models (e.g. AWC, SUC, AIC), relaxing the NP-hard selection ILP and rounding it, with continual online updates. It proves regret/violation bounds and evaluates on nine LLMs across three scenarios.
key_idea: Combinatorial bandit with budget constraints for selecting LLM subsets online.
relevance_rationale: Seed; principled online multi-LLM selection with cost constraints and regret guarantees.

title: Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification
summary: TRIPLE links prompt selection from a candidate pool to fixed-budget best-arm identification, so the number of LLM evaluations spent picking a prompt is explicitly bounded. Variants also select few-shot examples.
key_idea: Prompt selection as fixed-budget best arm identification.
relevance_rationale: Budgeted exploration for configuration choice; transferable to model/prompt config selection.

title: Which LLM to Play? Convergence-Aware Online Model Selection with Time-Increasing Bandits
models_studied: API LLMs vs fine-tuned small LLMs
summary: Studies online model selection when candidate models improve over time (e.g. a small model being fine-tuned), using a time-increasing bandit (TI-UCB) with change detection for convergence. Proves logarithmic regret and tests on classification and LLM selection.
key_idea: Increasing-then-converging bandit for choosing between costly API LLM and improving local model.
relevance_rationale: Directly models the API-vs-local-small-model decision under online learning.
found_via: OpenAlex title: online model selection LLM

title: PAK-UCB Contextual Bandit: An Online Learning Approach to Prompt-Aware Selection of Generative Models and LLMs
summary: PAK-UCB is a kernel contextual bandit that learns which generative model is best for each prompt, sharing context across arms and using random Fourier features for speed. Experiments mostly cover text-to-image and image-to-text generators.
key_idea: Prompt-aware kernel UCB for per-prompt generative model selection.
relevance_rationale: Online per-prompt model selection; evaluation mostly non-LLM.
found_via: OpenAlex title: online model selection LLM

title: A Multi-Armed Bandit Approach to Online Selection and Evaluation of Generative Models
summary: Frames sample-efficient online evaluation and selection of generative models as a bandit, with UCB algorithms for FD and IS metrics and regret bounds.
key_idea: UCB bandits to pick the best generative model with minimal samples.
relevance_rationale: Background on bandit-based online model evaluation; image domain.
found_via: OpenAlex title: online model selection bandits

title: Neural Bandit Based Optimal LLM Selection for a Pipeline of Subtasks
benchmarks: two real datasets (e.g. diagnosis extraction pipeline)
summary: Selects an LLM for each subtask in a sequential pipeline, where upstream outputs affect downstream success and cost, via a neural contextual bandit (Sequential Bandits) that needs no historical performance data. Proves sublinear regret and evaluates on two real datasets.
key_idea: Neural contextual bandits for per-step LLM choice in multi-stage pipelines.
relevance_rationale: Online learning of step-level model assignment in agent-like pipelines; directly on target.

title: Learning to Route LLMs from Bandit Feedback: One Policy, Many Trade-offs
cost_reduction_reported: outperforms strong offline routers by at least 12.46% and the largest LLM by at least 2.45%
summary: BaRP trains a router under the same partial-feedback restriction as deployment (only the chosen model's outcome is seen), as a contextual bandit over prompt features and a preference vector so the cost/quality trade-off is tunable at test time. It beats offline full-information routers.
key_idea: Train routers under bandit feedback with a tunable preference vector.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses routing from production-style partial feedback.

title: Reward-Based Online LLM Routing via NeuralUCB
cost_reduction_reported: substantially lower inference cost than max-quality reference with competitive reward (RouterBench, simulated online)
summary: Implements NeuralUCB for cost-aware routing and evaluates it in a simulated online setting on RouterBench, beating random and min-cost baselines on utility.
key_idea: NeuralUCB applied to cost-aware LLM routing.
relevance_rationale: Simple empirical baseline for neural bandit routing.

title: Lodestar: An Online-Learning LLM Inference Router
cost_reduction_reported: 1.41x lower average TTFT and 1.47x lower P99 TTFT vs prefix-cache/load-aware heuristic (public cloud GPU cluster)
summary: Lodestar routes inference requests to GPU instances using an online-trained reward predictor over per-request cluster snapshots, adapting continuously to workload and hardware changes; it integrates with vLLM and learns good policies within about 5 minutes.
key_idea: Online-learned request-to-instance routing for LLM serving.
relevance_rationale: Serving-level online routing (not model choice); supporting systems technique.

title: OrcaRouter: A Production-Oriented LLM Router with Hybrid Offline-Online Learning
cost_reduction_reported: 75.54% accuracy at USD 1.00 per 1,000 queries; ranked second on RouterArena (arena score 72.08)
summary: OrcaRouter fits per-arm ridge regressors offline from a full-information reward matrix on curated prompts, then deploys as a LinUCB contextual bandit that can keep learning from bandit feedback.
key_idea: Offline warm-start plus online LinUCB updates for a production-oriented router.
relevance_rationale: Practical hybrid offline-online router design with public leaderboard results.

title: ParetoBandit: Budget-Paced Adaptive Routing for Non-Stationary LLM Serving
cost_reduction_reported: budget compliance within 0.4%; up to +0.071 quality lift under price/quality shifts (1,824 prompts, three-model portfolio)
summary: ParetoBandit is an open-source cost-aware contextual-bandit router with an online primal-dual budget pacer and geometric forgetting to track price and quality drift, plus a hot-swap registry for adding models with budgeted exploration.
key_idea: Budget pacing plus forgetting for non-stationary bandit routing.
relevance_rationale: Addresses drift, pricing changes and new-model onboarding in live routing.

title: Online LLM Selection via Constrained Bandits with Time-Varying Demand
summary: Online LLM selection in edge-cloud systems under hard packing and soft covering constraints with time-varying demand; a confidence-bound algorithm with demand prediction gets sublinear regret and violation.
key_idea: Constrained bandits with demand forecasts for LLM selection.
relevance_rationale: Theory-heavy; synthetic evaluation only.

title: Online Multi-LLM Selection via Contextual Bandits under Unstructured Context Evolution
summary: Studies sequential LLM selection across multi-step query refinement, where the prompt changes in response to earlier outputs. A LinUCB-based algorithm with myopic regret guarantees, plus budget-aware and position-aware variants, needs no offline data.
key_idea: LinUCB for multi-turn LLM selection under evolving context.
relevance_rationale: Online routing over multi-turn interactions; relevant to multi-step settings.

title: Cost-Optimal LLM Routing with Limited User Feedback under User Satisfaction Guarantees
cost_reduction_reported: reduces operating cost by up to 2.2x over existing baselines while meeting SLA constraints
summary: SLARouter learns a cost-optimal routing policy online from the sparse, one-sided feedback available in production (e.g. complaints), with guarantees on cost optimality and SLA compliance, without per-benchmark tuning.
key_idea: Online routing from sparse production feedback with SLA guarantees.
relevance_rationale: Matches the production reality of limited feedback; cost-focused.
found_via: OpenAlex title: user feedback LLM routing

title: Drift-Aware LLM Routing with Sparse Contexts and Shared Budgets
summary: Formulates non-stationary budgeted routing with high-dimensional sparse contexts and drift in both request mix and model frontier; the algorithm uses a rolling audit window, pessimistic reward/optimistic cost estimates and online shadow prices, with regret bounds under bounded drift.
key_idea: Sparse, drift-aware contextual bandit routing with shared budgets and audit sampling.
relevance_rationale: Theory for drift and audit-rate trade-offs; highly relevant framing, little empirical evidence.

title: WISERouter: LLM Routing with Workload Budget Constraint
summary: WISERouter treats routing as a constrained contextual bandit with a workload-level (not per-query) budget, with an offline variant learning from historical interactions and an online variant with O(sqrt T) regret. Tested on RouterBench and SWE-Bench.
key_idea: Workload-level budgeted routing learned from logs or online exploration.
relevance_rationale: Bridges offline logs and online exploration under budget; includes agentic SWE-Bench.

title: Online Linear Programming for Multi-Objective Routing in LLM Serving
summary: Casts dispatch of requests to decode workers as online linear programming with bid-price control and warm-started dual updates, improving latency/throughput SLOs in the Vidur simulator.
key_idea: Online LP bid-price control for LLM request dispatch.
relevance_rationale: Serving-layer online optimization; background.

title: RoBoN: Routed Online Best-of-n for Test-Time Scaling with Multiple LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: up to 3.4% absolute accuracy gain over single-model best-of-n at compute parity
summary: RoBoN routes each best-of-n generation across a suite of models sequentially, choosing the next model from reward-model scores and agreement among responses; it is training-free and beats single-model best-of-n.
key_idea: Online routing within best-of-n across multiple LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Online, in-query model routing for test-time scaling.

title: LLM Routing with Dueling Feedback
summary: Formulates routing as contextual dueling bandits learned from pairwise preferences, using contrastively fine-tuned, cost-aware model embeddings and Feel-Good Thompson Sampling; lower regret on RouterBench and MixInstruct.
key_idea: Dueling-bandit LLM routing from pairwise preferences.
relevance_rationale: Fits preference-style production feedback (A/B choices).

title: Correlation-Aware Contextual Bandits with Surrogate Rewards for LLM Routing
summary: Contextual bandits for routing that exploit correlated arms and noisy surrogate rewards (e.g. judge scores), with a decoupled estimator that stays robust when surrogates are misspecified.
key_idea: Mix judge-style surrogate rewards with true bandit feedback safely.
relevance_rationale: Key for learning from traffic without ground truth: surrogate plus sparse true labels.

title: Online Learning with LLM Experts from Limited Feedback
summary: Online routing of prompts to LLM experts when only m << T feedback observations are allowed; gives regret bounds for full-information and bandit settings and learns strong policies from limited feedback.
key_idea: Bandit routing with a feedback (labeling) budget.
relevance_rationale: Models the cost of acquiring feedback in production.

title: CONCUR: A Framework for Continual Constrained and Unconstrained Routing
benchmarks: knowledge- and reasoning-intensive tasks (ID and OOD)
summary: CONCUR trains one predictor per computation strategy (model plus decoding method) so new strategies can be added without full retraining, supporting budgeted and unbudgeted routing in continual settings.
key_idea: Modular per-strategy predictors for continual routing as the model pool changes.
relevance_rationale: Handles model-pool churn cheaply; relevant to production non-stationarity.

title: Near-Optimal Online Deployment and Routing for Streaming LLMs
summary: StageRoute jointly decides which LLMs to deploy at maintenance windows and how to route each query among live models under budget and throughput constraints, with a near-optimal T^(2/3) regret.
key_idea: Hierarchical bandit for model deployment plus per-query routing.
relevance_rationale: Captures streaming model inventory churn in production.

title: From Deferral to Learning: Online In-Context Knowledge Distillation for LLM Cascades
cost_reduction_reported: reduces strong model calls by up to 48.05% and fees by up to 49.63%
summary: Inter-Cascade stores reusable problem-solving strategies produced by the strong model on deferred queries and retrieves them into the weak model's context, so the cascade improves online without fine-tuning.
key_idea: Online in-context distillation turns deferrals into reusable guidance.
relevance_rationale: Learning from live traffic to reduce escalations over time.

title: Cache & Distil: Optimising API Calls to Large Language Models
summary: Neural caching: a small student is continuously trained on LLM responses to live requests, and an active-learning style policy decides which requests go to the LLM. Margin sampling and query-by-committee work best across budgets.
key_idea: Online distillation plus active-learning deferral to cut API calls.
relevance_rationale: Directly uses live traffic to shift load to a cheaper model.

title: Eagle: Efficient Training-Free Router for Multi-LLM Inference
cost_reduction_reported: up to 23.52% AUC improvement; 100-200x faster incremental updates
summary: Eagle is a training-free router combining global and query-local ELO ratings built from pairwise comparisons; ratings update incrementally, making it suitable for high-volume online serving.
key_idea: ELO-based router with cheap online updates.
relevance_rationale: Lightweight online-updatable routing from preference feedback.

title: MixLLM: Dynamic Routing in Mixed Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: 97.25% of GPT-4's quality at 24.18% of the cost under the time constraint
summary: MixLLM is a contextual-bandit routing system with lightweight quality/cost predictors and a meta-decision maker balancing quality, cost and latency; it trains continually from user feedback and handles LLMs being added or removed.
key_idea: Contextual-bandit router with continual learning and dynamic model pool.
relevance_rationale: Reports strong cost-quality numbers and supports continual learning in deployment.

title: LASeR: Learning to Adaptively Select Reward Models with Multi-Armed Bandits
cost_reduction_reported: about 2x speedup vs RM ensemble
summary: LASeR picks which reward model to use per instance with a multi-armed bandit during iterative LLM training, beating RM ensembles in accuracy and efficiency.
key_idea: Bandit selection among reward models.
relevance_rationale: Bandit selection of evaluators; background.

title: Cost-aware LLM-based Online Dataset Annotation
summary: CaMVo selects, per item, a subset of LLMs for majority-vote labeling with LinUCB and a Bayesian confidence estimator, matching full majority voting at lower cost without ground-truth labels.
key_idea: LinUCB subset selection for cheaper LLM ensembles.
relevance_rationale: Label-free online model-subset selection.

title: A Component-Based Survey of Interactions between Large Language Models and Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Survey of how bandit algorithms help LLM systems (from pretraining to RAG and personalization) and how LLMs help bandits, organized by component; with a curated GitHub list.
key_idea: Component-level survey of LLM-bandit interactions.
relevance_rationale: Useful map of bandit methods applied to LLMs.

title: Dynamic Model Routing and Cascading for Efficient LLM Inference: A Survey
summary: Survey of dynamic model routing and cascading, organizing systems by when routing decisions are made, what information they use and how they are computed.
key_idea: Taxonomy survey of routing and cascades.
relevance_rationale: Survey covering online and offline routing.

title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
summary: Describes the Chatbot Arena platform, which collects crowdsourced pairwise votes between LLMs on real user prompts (over 240K votes at time of writing) and ranks models with Bradley-Terry style statistics.
key_idea: Live crowdsourced pairwise preference collection for LLM ranking.
relevance_rationale: Canonical source of online preference data used to train routers (e.g. RouteLLM).

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
summary: Shows strong LLM judges (GPT-4) agree with human preferences over 80% of the time, similar to human-human agreement, using MT-Bench and early Chatbot Arena data; releases votes and conversations.
key_idea: LLM-as-a-judge validated against crowdsourced preferences.
relevance_rationale: Judge signal and Arena data underpin router training and online evaluation.

title: Prediction-Powered Ranking of Large Language Models
summary: Combines a small set of human pairwise comparisons with many LLM-judge comparisons via prediction-powered inference to give rank-sets with coverage guarantees; finds judge-only rankings often inconsistent with human preference.
key_idea: Statistically valid ranking from few human plus many judge labels.
relevance_rationale: Method to combine cheap judge labels with scarce human feedback, applicable to router evaluation.

title: Elo Uncovered: Robustness and Best Practices in Language Model Evaluation
summary: Tests whether Elo ratings for LLMs satisfy reliability and transitivity and finds they often do not, giving guidance on hyperparameters and practice.
key_idea: Elo-based LLM evaluation is volatile; best practices.
relevance_rationale: Background for preference-based online evaluation.

title: Simulating Bandit Learning from User Feedback for Extractive Question Answering
summary: Simulates contextual-bandit learning from user feedback on extractive QA, showing models trained on few examples improve substantially from feedback and can adapt to new domains without annotation.
key_idea: Bandit learning from simulated user feedback in QA.
relevance_rationale: Background on learning from deployment feedback.

title: Continually Improving Extractive QA via Human Feedback
summary: Deploys an extractive QA system and improves it iteratively from thousands of real user feedback interactions, showing gains over time including domain adaptation.
key_idea: Continual improvement from real deployed-user feedback.
relevance_rationale: Real feedback loop evidence; not cost-focused.

title: Learning New Skills after Deployment: Improving open-domain internet-driven dialogue with human feedback
summary: Collects deployment interactions with several kinds of human feedback and compares learning algorithms (supervised, rejection sampling, Director, reward-based) for improving dialogue models; releases the data.
key_idea: Which feedback types and algorithms work for post-deployment improvement.
relevance_rationale: Background on learning from production feedback.

title: WildFeedback: Aligning LLMs With In-situ User Interactions And Feedback
summary: Mines in-situ user satisfaction and dissatisfaction signals from real conversations to build preference data for aligning LLMs.
key_idea: Implicit feedback in real chat logs as preference labels.
relevance_rationale: Shows how to extract labels from production conversations.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
summary: Adaptive conformal inference keeps long-run coverage of prediction sets online under arbitrary distribution shift by updating one miscoverage parameter over time.
key_idea: Online conformal calibration under drift.
relevance_rationale: Tool for keeping router/cascade thresholds calibrated under drift.

title: Steering Frozen LLMs: Adaptive Social Alignment via Online Prompt Routing
summary: CCLUB routes queries among system prompts with a consensus-clustering LinUCB bandit to adapt safety alignment at inference time, with sublinear regret.
key_idea: Clustered LinUCB routing across system prompts.
relevance_rationale: Online configuration routing, safety not cost.

title: POLAR: Online Learning for LoRA Adapter Caching and Routing in Edge LLM Serving
summary: Two-timescale online control of which LoRA adapters stay in GPU memory and how requests are routed to adapters, with contextual-bandit regret guarantees.
key_idea: Bandit routing plus caching of LoRA adapters.
relevance_rationale: Serving-level online routing background.

title: PROTEUS: SLA-Aware Routing via Lagrangian RL for Multi-LLM Serving Systems
cost_reduction_reported: cost savings reach 89.8% versus the best fixed model; 90.1% accuracy on RouterBench within 1.3% of oracle
summary: PROTEUS trains a Lagrangian-RL router conditioned on an operator-specified accuracy floor, so one model meets a range of targets without retraining; beats OmniRouter on floor compliance.
key_idea: SLA-target-conditioned router via Lagrangian RL.
relevance_rationale: Operator-facing accuracy targets; strong cost numbers.

title: Use Your INSTINCT: INSTruction optimization for LLMs usIng Neural bandits Coupled with Transformers
summary: INSTINCT optimizes instructions for black-box LLMs with a neural bandit whose surrogate uses a pre-trained transformer's representations.
key_idea: Neural-bandit instruction optimization.
relevance_rationale: Bandit configuration search background.

title: A contextual-bandit approach to personalized news article recommendation
summary: Introduces LinUCB for personalized news recommendation on Yahoo! traffic, a contextual bandit with linear payoff and upper-confidence exploration.
key_idea: LinUCB contextual bandit.
relevance_rationale: Foundational algorithm used by PILOT, OrcaRouter and others.

title: Bandits with Knapsacks
summary: Defines bandits with knapsacks, where each pull consumes budgeted resources, and gives near-optimal algorithms (balanced exploration and primal-dual).
key_idea: Bandits under budget constraints.
relevance_rationale: Foundation for budget-constrained routing.

title: Resourceful Contextual Bandits
summary: Extends bandits with knapsacks to contextual bandits over general policy classes with near-optimal regret.
key_idea: Contextual bandits with resource constraints.
relevance_rationale: Background for budgeted contextual routing.

title: Linear Contextual Bandits with Knapsacks
summary: Linear contextual bandits with knapsack constraints, generalizing LinUCB and BwK, with near-optimal regret.
key_idea: Linear contextual BwK.
relevance_rationale: Direct template for budgeted LinUCB routing.

title: Neural Contextual Bandits with UCB-based Exploration
summary: NeuralUCB uses neural-network features to build upper confidence bounds with near-optimal regret for contextual bandits.
key_idea: Neural contextual bandits with UCB.
relevance_rationale: Algorithm used by neural bandit routers.

title: Neural Thompson Sampling
summary: Neural Thompson Sampling uses a neural-network posterior mean with neural-tangent-feature variance for contextual bandits.
key_idea: Neural Thompson sampling.
relevance_rationale: Background algorithm.

title: Analysis of Thompson Sampling for the multi-armed bandit problem
summary: First logarithmic regret analysis of Thompson Sampling for the multi-armed bandit.
key_idea: Regret guarantees for Thompson sampling.
relevance_rationale: Foundational TS reference.

title: A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling
summary: Tutorial on Thompson sampling covering Bernoulli bandits, recommendation, assortment and RL, with guidance on when it works.
key_idea: Thompson sampling tutorial.
relevance_rationale: Background for TS-based routers.

title: Non-stationary Bandits with Knapsacks
summary: Studies bandits with knapsacks in non-stationary environments, proposing a global non-stationarity measure and primal-dual bounds.
key_idea: Non-stationary BwK.
relevance_rationale: Theory for budgeted routing under drift.

title: Agentic Routing: The Harness-Native Data Flywheel
summary: Argues model selection inside agent harnesses should be learned from logged execution records (query, harness state, model choice, trace, outcome, cost) whose labels come from the environment; implements a four-layer routing stack with a LightGBM cold-start ranker in OpenSquilla.
key_idea: Agent execution traces as a data flywheel for routers.
relevance_rationale: Directly on target: learning agent-level routing from logged traces.

title: Learning Agent Routing From Early Experience
cost_reduction_reported: reduces inference time by 60.6% vs agent while improving performance by 28.6% over direct LLM inference
summary: BoundaryRouter decides whether to answer with a direct LLM call or escalate to a full agent, using an experience memory built by running both on a seed set and retrieving similar cases.
key_idea: Route between plain LLM and full agent from early experience.
relevance_rationale: Cost-aware LLM-vs-agent escalation using small logged experience.

title: AgentRouter: Heterogeneous Model Routing for Cost-Optimal Multi-Step Agentic Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: 72% cost reduction vs frontier-only baseline retaining 97.3% of frontier-only quality
summary: AgentRouter maps each agent trajectory step to one of four model tiers using features available at routing time, trained on 50,000 annotated steps; beats per-step RouteLLM and FrugalGPT.
key_idea: Step-level model-tier routing learned from annotated trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence for per-step downscaling in agent workflows.

title: Routing Should Pay for Itself: Sparse Supervision for Economical LLM Routing
cost_reduction_reported: uses about 33-41% of training feedback; reduces break-even deployment volume by about 1.9-9.5x
summary: Accounts for the upfront cost of collecting query-model feedback to train a router, and learns from sparse supervision so routing savings pay back sooner.
key_idea: Router supervision cost vs serving savings break-even.
relevance_rationale: Economic framing of offline router data collection.

title: RLCascadeRouter: Quality-Estimator-Free Cascade Routing via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Formulates cascade routing (stop or call another model) as an MDP optimized by RL without separate quality estimators; handles unseen models without retraining.
key_idea: RL cascade routing without quality estimators.
relevance_rationale: RL-trained cascade policy from offline data.

title: Expected Reward Prediction, with Applications to Model Routing
summary: Shows the expected reward an LLM would earn on a prompt under repeated sampling can be predicted before generation, and uses this prediction for cost-controlled routing that beats category-level baselines.
key_idea: Predict expected reward-model score per model per prompt for routing.
relevance_rationale: Reward modeling for routing, extensible to new models.

title: From Production Traffic to Post-Training: Building a Self-Hosted LLM That Covers the Corporate Request Mix
cost_reduction_reported: model absorbs 50% of platform traffic (116M requests/month) at a fraction of the serving cost
summary: Consolidates traffic from over 200 internal applications onto one self-hosted model by analyzing production errors, training per-axis GRPO experts and merging them; benchmarks are stratified to production traffic.
key_idea: Production-traffic-driven post-training to replace a larger model fleet.
relevance_rationale: Rare production evidence of using logs to cut serving cost.

title: Prompt Optimization with Logged Bandit Data
benchmarks: new benchmark suite: personalized movie descriptions
summary: Optimizes which prompt an LLM pipeline uses for personalized sentence generation from naturally logged user feedback (clicks), with a kernel-based off-policy gradient that exploits similarity between generated sentences to cut variance while limiting bias.
key_idea: Off-policy prompt-policy learning from logged bandit feedback.
relevance_rationale: Direct OPE/OPL applied to LLM configuration choice from production-style logs.
found_via: OpenAlex title search (seed: Kiyohara/Saito OPE for language generation)

title: An Off-Policy Learning Approach for Steering Sentence Generation towards Personalization
summary: RecSys 2025 paper by Kiyohara, Cao, Saito and Joachims proposing an off-policy learning approach to steer LLM sentence generation toward personalization using logged feedback (abstract not retrieved; details from title and author record only).
key_idea: Off-policy learning for steering personalized LLM generation.
relevance_rationale: OPE/OPL for LLM generation from logged data; companion to the prompt-optimization paper.
found_via: OpenAlex title: off-policy learning personalized generation

title: Off-Policy Evaluation from Logged Human Feedback
summary: Formalizes evaluating a new model using human feedback logged on another model's responses, proposing model-based and model-free estimators that estimate absolute policy values, rank policies, and can be optimized.
key_idea: OPE of LLM policies from logged human feedback.
relevance_rationale: Exactly the tool for evaluating a candidate routing/config policy on existing labeled logs.

title: OTROPE: Optimal Transport-based Robust Off-policy Evaluation for Large Language Models
benchmarks: synthetic and real LLM evaluation tasks
summary: OTROPE evaluates a new target LLM using scarce human labels collected on a behavior LLM, aligning samples in semantic space via optimal transport and combining corrected residuals with proxy predictors in a doubly-robust style, without needing response likelihoods.
key_idea: Optimal-transport doubly-robust OPE for black-box LLMs.
relevance_rationale: OPE for swapping models when likelihoods are unavailable (API models).

title: Pluralistic Off-policy Evaluation and Alignment
summary: Extends off-policy evaluation to pluralistic preference alignment with decomposable IPS estimators for relevance and diversity, and uses them for off-policy optimization of LLM responses.
key_idea: Decomposed IPS OPE for pluralistic LLM alignment.
relevance_rationale: OPE machinery for LLMs from logged preference data.

title: OCEAN: Offline Chain-of-thought Evaluation and Alignment in Large Language Models
summary: OCEAN performs offline evaluation of chain-of-thought using knowledge-graph feedback and a KG-IPS estimator with unbiasedness guarantees, then optimizes the LLM off-policy.
key_idea: IPS-based offline evaluation of LLM reasoning paths.
relevance_rationale: Shows IPS/OPE adapted to LLM outputs.

title: Off-Policy Evaluation for Large Action Spaces via Embeddings
summary: Proposes an OPE estimator using marginalized importance weights over action embeddings, which avoids IPS collapse when the action space is huge, as with language outputs.
key_idea: Marginalized IPS via action embeddings for large action spaces.
relevance_rationale: Foundational estimator for OPE over many LLMs/prompts/responses.

title: Open Bandit Dataset and Pipeline: Towards Realistic and Reproducible Off-Policy Evaluation
summary: Releases a real logged bandit dataset from a large fashion e-commerce platform collected under multiple policies, plus Open Bandit Pipeline, a library implementing OPE estimators and batch bandit algorithms.
key_idea: Real multi-policy logged data and a reference OPE library.
relevance_rationale: Tooling reusable for OPE of routing policies.

title: Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation and Learning
summary: Applies doubly robust estimation to contextual-bandit policy evaluation and optimization, giving accurate estimates when either the reward model or the logging-policy model is good.
key_idea: Doubly robust off-policy evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Core estimator for counterfactual evaluation of routers from logs.

title: Counterfactual Risk Minimization: Learning from Logged Bandit Feedback
summary: Introduces counterfactual risk minimization for batch learning from logged bandit feedback, with variance-aware generalization bounds and the POEM algorithm.
key_idea: Counterfactual risk minimization (POEM).
relevance_rationale: Foundation for learning a router from logged partial feedback.

title: The self-normalized estimator for counterfactual learning
venue_or_source: Conference paper (2015; venue per OpenAlex not listed)
summary: Identifies a propensity-overfitting problem in the standard counterfactual risk estimator and proposes the self-normalized estimator (SNIPS) to avoid it in batch learning from logged bandit feedback.
key_idea: Self-normalized IPS estimator.
relevance_rationale: Standard low-variance OPE estimator.

title: Deep Learning with Logged Bandit Feedback
summary: BanditNet trains deep networks from logged contextual bandit feedback using a CRM objective with an equivariant, self-normalized estimator.
key_idea: Deep learning from logged bandit feedback.
relevance_rationale: Template for training neural routers on logged traffic.

title: Counterfactual Reasoning and Learning Systems
summary: Uses causal inference on logged data to predict how changes to a complex learning system (Bing ad placement) would affect performance, before deploying them.
key_idea: Counterfactual reasoning on production logs.
relevance_rationale: Classic production example of counterfactual system tuning.

title: Offline A/B Testing for Recommender Systems
summary: Proposes a counterfactual estimator with a modeled bias for offline A/B testing of recommender systems and benchmarks estimators against real online A/B results.
key_idea: Offline A/B testing validated against online A/B tests.
relevance_rationale: Shows how OPE correlates with production A/B outcomes.

title: Unbiased Offline Evaluation of Contextual-bandit-based News Article Recommendation Algorithms
summary: Introduces a replay method for provably unbiased offline evaluation of contextual-bandit algorithms from randomly logged traffic, validated against online bucket tests at Yahoo!.
key_idea: Replay evaluation of bandit policies from logs.
relevance_rationale: Simple method to evaluate online routers offline if some traffic is randomized.

title: Doubly Robust Off-Policy Evaluation for Ranking Policies under the Cascade Behavior Model
summary: Cascade doubly robust estimator for off-policy evaluation of ranking policies, reducing variance under a top-down user behavior assumption.
key_idea: Cascade-DR OPE for rankings.
relevance_rationale: OPE for sequential decisions, analogous to cascades.

title: Towards Automatic Evaluation of Dialog Systems: A Model-Free Off-Policy Evaluation Approach
summary: ENIGMA estimates human evaluation scores for dialog systems via model-free off-policy evaluation using only a small amount of pre-collected experience data.
key_idea: OPE to evaluate dialog policies without live humans.
relevance_rationale: Early OPE for language systems.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback in Real-World Sequence-to-Sequence Tasks
summary: Position paper on offline RL from interaction logs of deployed NLP systems, covering practical challenges (e.g. deterministic logging, reliability of feedback) and possible solutions.
key_idea: Offline RL from deployed NLP system logs: challenges.
relevance_rationale: Background on learning from production logs.

title: Offline Regularised Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models Alignment
summary: DRO optimizes an LLM from single-trajectory data (prompt, response, user thumbs up/down) with a mean-squared objective, avoiding the need for pairwise preferences; outperforms KTO.
key_idea: Learn from abundant single-response user feedback logs.
relevance_rationale: Relevant to using production feedback, though for alignment not routing.

title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
cost_reduction_reported: reduces costs by over 2 times in certain cases without compromising response quality
summary: Trains strong-vs-weak routers from Chatbot Arena human preference data with augmentation, and shows routers transfer when the model pair changes. Companion LMSYS blog.
key_idea: Routers trained on logged human preference data.
relevance_rationale: Canonical example of training a router from logged preference data.

title: Arch-Router: Aligning LLM Routing with Human Preferences
summary: Arch-Router is a 1.5B model that maps queries to user-defined domain/action preference policies for routing, so new models can be added without retraining; claims SOTA preference matching on conversational data.
key_idea: Preference-aligned router using human-defined policies.
relevance_rationale: Industry router (Katanemo) that encodes operator preferences.

title: FusionFactory: Fusing LLM Capabilities with Multi-LLM Log Data
summary: Builds LLMFusionBench from responses of 20 open LLMs (103M tokens) and shows multi-LLM logs can train query-level routers, retrieve reasoning templates, and distill from top responses to beat the best single LLM.
key_idea: Multi-LLM logs as training data for routing and fusion.
relevance_rationale: Directly uses logged multi-model outputs to learn routing.

title: SeqRoute: Global Budget-Aware Sequential LLM Routing via Offline Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: reduces operational costs by 6.0-73.5% while maintaining or improving quality; bankruptcy rates under 1%
summary: SeqRoute formulates multi-turn routing under a session-level budget as a finite-horizon MDP learned by offline RL, with hindsight budget relabeling to augment logged sessions.
key_idea: Offline RL over logged sessions for budget-aware multi-turn routing.
relevance_rationale: Offline RL from logs with global budgets; close to agent-level settings.
found_via: OpenAlex title: offline reinforcement learning routing LLM

title: Efficient Contextual LLM Cascades through Budget-Constrained Policy Learning
cost_reduction_reported: cost savings of up to 85% compared to baselines while maintaining high accuracy
summary: TREACLE is an RL policy that jointly chooses the LLM and prompting scheme per question under long-term monetary and latency budgets, using question embeddings and the consistency of earlier responses.
key_idea: RL policy for joint model and prompt selection under budgets.
relevance_rationale: Budgeted policy learning for cascades.

title: LMSYS-Chat-1M: A Large-Scale Real-World LLM Conversation Dataset
summary: Releases one million real conversations with 25 LLMs collected from the Vicuna demo and Chatbot Arena, with use cases such as moderation models and benchmark building.
key_idea: Large real-world LLM conversation log dataset.
relevance_rationale: Public proxy for production traffic to train/evaluate routers.

title: WildChat: 1M ChatGPT Interaction Logs in the Wild
summary: WildChat is a corpus of 1M opt-in user-ChatGPT conversations (over 2.5M turns) with timestamps and demographic metadata.
key_idea: Real-world ChatGPT interaction logs.
relevance_rationale: Public production-like logs for router training and analysis.

title: From Crowdsourced Data to High-Quality Benchmarks: Arena-Hard and BenchBuilder Pipeline
cost_reduction_reported: Arena-Hard-Auto: 3x higher separation than MT-Bench, 98.6% correlation with human preference rankings, at a cost of $20
summary: BenchBuilder curates hard prompts from crowdsourced logs (Chatbot Arena, WildChat) and scores them with LLM judges, producing Arena-Hard-Auto.
key_idea: Turning logged traffic into a cheap, human-aligned eval set.
relevance_rationale: Method for building offline evals from production-like logs.

title: PredictaBoard: Benchmarking LLM Score Predictability
summary: PredictaBoard benchmarks assessors that predict whether an LLM will fail on a given prompt, scoring LLM-assessor pairs by rejection rate at different error tolerances.
key_idea: Benchmark for instance-level LLM success prediction.
relevance_rationale: Instance-level performance predictors are the core of predictive routers.

title: Predicting Emergent Capabilities by Finetuning
summary: Predicts whether future larger models will show emergent capability on a task by fine-tuning smaller models with varying data and fitting emergence laws.
key_idea: Emergence prediction via fine-tuning.
relevance_rationale: Background on capability prediction.

title: Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Language Model Performance
summary: Builds scaling laws from about 100 public models via a low-dimensional capability space, predicting emergent behavior and agent performance from simpler benchmarks.
key_idea: Observational scaling laws for predicting LLM performance.
relevance_rationale: Predicting agentic performance from cheap benchmarks helps model choice.

title: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
cost_reduction_reported: estimate MMLU (14K examples) performance from 100 curated examples
summary: Shows small curated subsets (e.g. 100 MMLU items) plus IRT-based estimators can reproduce full-benchmark LLM results; releases tiny benchmark versions.
key_idea: Estimate full-benchmark performance from ~100 items.
relevance_rationale: Cheap evaluation of candidate models/configs before switching.

title: Efficient multi-prompt evaluation of LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: estimates performance quantiles across 100 prompt templates on MMLU with a budget of two single-prompt evaluations
summary: PromptEval estimates an LLM's performance distribution across many prompt templates under small evaluation budgets by sharing strength across prompts and examples.
key_idea: Budgeted estimation of performance over prompt variants.
relevance_rationale: Efficient offline evaluation for configuration choice.

title: Anchor Points: Benchmarking Models with Much Fewer Examples
summary: Anchor Point Selection picks tiny subsets whose model confidences represent the whole dataset, reliably ranking models and estimating per-point predictions.
key_idea: Rank models from 1-30 anchor examples.
relevance_rationale: Background on cheap evaluation.

title: How Predictable Are Large Language Model Capabilities? A Case Study on BIG-bench
signals_used: experiment records: model family, size, task, shots
summary: Trains an MLP on BIG-bench experiment records to predict LLM performance on new configurations (R^2 > 95% on random splits) and searches for a small informative task subset.
key_idea: Performance prediction from past experiment records.
relevance_rationale: Predicting configuration performance from logs of past runs.

title: Collaborative Performance Prediction for Large Language Models
summary: Collaborative Performance Prediction treats model-by-task scores like a recommender matrix, using historical results and design factors to predict LLM downstream performance better than scaling laws.
key_idea: Collaborative filtering for LLM performance prediction.
relevance_rationale: Recsys-style prediction of which model will do well.

title: Can We Predict Performance of Large Models across Vision-Language Tasks?
summary: Predicts unknown model-by-dataset scores for vision-language models via probabilistic matrix factorization with MCMC uncertainty, using uncertainty to prioritize which evaluations to run.
key_idea: Matrix completion with uncertainty for performance prediction.
relevance_rationale: Background; vision-language focus.

title: Predicting Language Models' Success at Zero-Shot Probabilistic Prediction
summary: Large study of LLM zero-shot probabilistic prediction on tabular tasks; builds label-free metrics that predict at the task level whether an LLM will do well.
key_idea: Label-free task-level prediction of LLM suitability.
relevance_rationale: Background on predicting LLM success without labels.
found_via: OpenAlex title: predicting success language model

title: Predictable Artificial Intelligence
summary: Position paper defining Predictable AI: anticipating validity indicators such as performance and safety of AI systems, and the candidate predictors and trade-offs involved.
key_idea: Framework for predicting AI performance.
relevance_rationale: Conceptual background for assessor-based routing.

title: Generalized Correctness Models: Learning Calibrated and Model-Agnostic Correctness Predictors from Historical Patterns
summary: Trains correctness predictors on historical correctness data across many models and finds they generalize across models, suggesting confidence estimation is learnable from history rather than self-introspection.
key_idea: Model-agnostic correctness predictors from logged outcomes.
relevance_rationale: Predict success of any model from historical logs, key for routers.

title: No Answer Needed: Predicting LLM Answer Accuracy from Question-Only Linear Probes
summary: Linear probes on activations after reading a question, before generation, predict whether the model's answer will be correct, generalizing out of distribution except on math.
key_idea: Pre-generation correctness probes.
relevance_rationale: Cheap pre-generation success signal for routing/cascades.

title: Predicting LLM Reasoning Performance with Small Proxy Model
signals_used: small proxy model NLL weighted by task alignment
cost_reduction_reported: reduces dataset ranking costs by over 100x relative to the best baseline
summary: rBridge uses small (<=1B) proxy models with task-aligned likelihood to predict larger models' reasoning performance for pretraining data decisions.
key_idea: Small proxies predict large-model reasoning.
relevance_rationale: Background on performance prediction.

title: How Benchmark Prediction from Fewer Data Misses the Mark
summary: Evaluates 11 benchmark-prediction methods on 19 benchmarks and finds they mostly interpolate among similar models and fail to beat random sampling when extrapolating to stronger new models; proposes an AIPW-based method with modest gains.
key_idea: Benchmark prediction fails at the frontier.
relevance_rationale: Important caution for predicting new-model performance offline.

title: Confidence Before Answering: A Paradigm Shift for Efficient LLM Uncertainty Estimation
summary: CoCA trains models with GRPO to output a calibrated confidence before answering, jointly optimizing calibration and accuracy.
key_idea: Confidence-first outputs trained with RL.
relevance_rationale: Pre-answer confidence can drive routing/escalation.

title: Large Language Model Routing with Benchmark Datasets
summary: Repurposes existing benchmark datasets to learn routers that pick the best LLM for new tasks, reducing the problem to per-model binary correctness classifiers.
key_idea: Train routers from benchmark correctness records.
relevance_rationale: Early performance-prediction router from offline data.

title: Fly-Swat or Cannon? Cost-Effective Language Model Choice via Meta-Modeling
cost_reduction_reported: match the performance of the largest LM while achieving a cost reduction of 63% (14 datasets, four LMs)
summary: FORC trains a meta-model to predict each LM's performance on an input and assigns inputs to models under a budget, with a public library.
key_idea: Meta-model performance prediction for cost-aware LM assignment.
relevance_rationale: Clear cost numbers from predictive routing.

title: Routing to the Expert: Efficient Reward-guided Ensemble of Large Language Models
summary: Zooter distills reward-model scores on training queries into a routing function so each query goes to the best LLM, avoiding expensive ensemble reranking.
key_idea: Reward-model-distilled router.
relevance_rationale: Reward models as synthetic labels for router training.

title: IRT-Router: Effective and Interpretable Multi-LLM Routing via Item Response Theory
summary: IRT-Router models LLM ability and query difficulty with item response theory to predict response performance, with an online warm-up for cold-start queries.
key_idea: Item response theory for predictive routing.
relevance_rationale: Interpretable performance prediction for routing.

title: EmbedLLM: Learning Compact Representations of Large Language Models
summary: EmbedLLM learns compact vector representations of LLMs from their correctness patterns, enabling routing and forecasting benchmark performance without extra inference.
key_idea: Model embeddings for routing and performance forecasting.
relevance_rationale: Reusable representations for predicting which model succeeds.

title: Rethinking Predictive Modeling for LLM Routing: When Simple kNN Beats Complex Learned Routers
summary: Shows a well-tuned kNN router matches or beats complex learned routers because model performance is local in embedding space.
key_idea: kNN over logged outcomes is a strong router baseline.
relevance_rationale: Simple, data-efficient baseline for learning from logs.

title: CARROT: A Cost Aware Rate Optimal Router
summary: Minimax analysis shows a router that predicts both cost and accuracy per question can be rate-optimal; CARROT implements this and SPROUT is released as a price-aware routing dataset.
key_idea: Minimax-optimal predict-cost-and-accuracy router.
relevance_rationale: Theory supporting performance-prediction routing.

title: Universal Model Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
signals_used: LLM feature vector from representative prompts
summary: UniRoute represents each LLM by its predictions on a representative prompt set, allowing routing among previously unseen LLMs via cluster-based rules with excess-risk bounds.
key_idea: Routing to unseen LLMs via prompt-set profiles.
relevance_rationale: Handles model-pool churn with a small profiling cost.

title: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
cost_reduction_reported: up to 40% fewer calls to the large model with no drop in response quality
summary: Trains a router predicting whether the small model's answer will match the large model's, with a tunable quality threshold at test time.
key_idea: Quality-gap prediction for small/large routing.
relevance_rationale: Performance prediction to save large-model calls.

title: Offline Learning for Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits
summary: Off-CMAB learns combinatorial bandit policies from offline logs with a pessimistic lower-confidence-bound algorithm, with applications including LLM caching.
key_idea: Offline pessimistic learning for combinatorial bandits.
relevance_rationale: Learning from logs instead of costly online exploration.

title: Doubly Robust Alignment for Large Language Models
summary: Doubly robust preference optimization for RLHF that stays consistent if either the preference model or the reference policy is correct.
key_idea: Doubly robust RLHF.
relevance_rationale: OPE-style robustness in LLM training; background.

title: Probabilities of Chat LLMs Are Miscalibrated but Still Predict Correctness on Multiple-Choice Q&A
summary: Finds chat LLM maximum softmax probabilities are miscalibrated but still predict correctness, and uses them for selective abstention with little labeled data.
key_idea: Softmax confidence predicts correctness despite miscalibration.
relevance_rationale: Cheap correctness signal.

title: Learning to Route LLMs from Implicit Cost-Performance Preferences via Meta-Learning
summary: MetaRouter learns each user's implicit cost-performance preference from a few interactions by treating preference profiles as tasks in a meta-learned contextual bandit.
key_idea: Meta-learned bandit router for per-user preferences.
relevance_rationale: Online learning of user-specific cost trade-offs.

title: The Coverage Illusion: From Pre-retrieval Routing Failure to Post-retrieval Cascades in a Production RAG System
cost_reduction_reported: serves 72.2% of real user queries without LLM augmentation; latency reduced 31.8%
summary: Production case study (Danish National Encyclopedia): synthetic queries mislead routing for RAG query augmentation, pre-retrieval routers fail, and a cheapest-first post-retrieval cascade improves quality and latency on real traffic.
key_idea: Synthetic vs real traffic mismatch; post-retrieval cascade.
relevance_rationale: Production evidence that offline synthetic data misleads routers.

title: Towards Optimizing the Costs of LLM Usage
cost_reduction_reported: reduce costs by 40%-90% while improving quality by 4%-7%
summary: Predicts LLM output quality without generating, then solves cost-quality optimization for model choice, plus token-reduction via sentence simplification; validated on enterprise document-processing data.
key_idea: Quality prediction plus optimization for enterprise LLM cost.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise data evidence for predictive model selection.

title: Optimising Calls to Large Language Models with Uncertainty-Based Two-Tier Selection
cost_reduction_reported: outperforms existing methods on 25 out of 27 experimental setups
summary: Uses only the small LLM's generation uncertainty to decide whether to call the large LLM, outperforming routers and cascades that need extra neural models.
key_idea: Uncertainty-only two-tier selection.
relevance_rationale: Strong simple cascade baseline.

title: Large-scale validation and analysis of interleaved search evaluation
summary: Comprehensive empirical analysis of interleaving, which compares two rankers by mixing their results and counting user clicks, using data from two commercial search engines; shows it is efficient and agrees with other evaluations.
key_idea: Interleaving as sensitive online comparison from implicit feedback.
relevance_rationale: Background for online comparison of LLM configurations with implicit feedback.

title: Online controlled experiments at large scale
summary: Describes running hundreds of concurrent online controlled experiments at Bing and the cultural, engineering and trustworthiness challenges involved.
key_idea: A/B testing practice at scale.
relevance_rationale: Reference practice for A/B testing LLM routing changes.

title: Chatbot Arena Estimate: towards a generalized performance benchmark for LLM capabilities
summary: Industry-track paper proposing a way to estimate Chatbot Arena-style performance as a general benchmark for LLM capabilities (abstract not retrieved; described from title and venue only).
key_idea: Estimating Arena scores as a benchmark.
relevance_rationale: Performance prediction from preference data; limited detail verified.

title: metabench -- A Sparse Benchmark of Reasoning and Knowledge in Large Language Models
signals_used: item-level accuracies from Open LLM Leaderboard
summary: Builds a sparse benchmark from item-wise accuracies of many models on six Open LLM Leaderboard benchmarks, selecting a small item subset that predicts full benchmark scores.
key_idea: Small item subsets predict full-benchmark performance.
relevance_rationale: Background on cheap evaluation for model selection.
found_via: OpenAlex title: metabench; verified via arXiv id lookup
